meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition; commercial law codified in the Code de commerce)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF) Arts. L.561-1 to L.561-50 and R.561-1 et seq.; CMF Art. L.561-2-2 and Decree No. 2018-284 of 19 April 2018 (French beneficial-owner register); Ordinance No. 2016-1635 of 1 December 2016 (AMLD4 transposition); AMLD5 and AMLD6 via successive amendments; Code de commerce Art. L.227-1 et seq. (SAS rules) and Art. L.561-45; Tracfin declaration duties under CMF Art. L.561-15; EU Regulations 269/2014 and 833/2014 (restrictive measures).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each UBO and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or issuing consulate/embassy in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Hague Convention members) OR French Consular Legalization (for non-Hague countries such as China, UAE, Qatar)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and recent registry extract (good standing) of each corporate shareholder of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR French Consular Legalization, followed by sworn translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and manager (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or issuing bank, with notarized signature certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing origin of funds and existing banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating bank in the parent-company country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization when required under the receiving French bank's KYC policy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn translation certificate for all non-French documents (passports, certificates, bank documents)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-certified translator (traducteur assermenté) registered on the court list
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; translator's official seal and declaration attached

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory multi-list screening of all UBOs, managers, and material counterparties prior to incorporation: (i) PEP classification under CMF R.561-18-3 and EU AMLD5; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists; (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (Gelsomino), including Regulations 269/2014 and 833/2014; (iv) OFAC SDN, SSI, and sectoral lists; (v) UK HMT consolidated sanctions; (vi) Tracfin advisories and FATF high-risk jurisdiction monitoring. Continuous re-screening at intervals not exceeding 90 days and a five-year documentary retention standard are applied.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; ancillary name-conflict verification via the RCS database operated by the greffes des tribunaux de commerce (Infogreffe) and the INPI data.inpi trademark module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be written in Latin script; names in Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese, or other scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters in the articles and in the RCS filing. The legal form 'Société par actions simplifiée' or its abbreviation 'SAS' must appear in the articles and in all commercial documents. A name must not be confusingly similar to a pre-existing registered business name in the same activity class (Art. L.711-2 Code de la propriété intellectuelle) and must not contain prohibited or misleading tokens.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / établissement de crédit / société de financement (prior ACPR authorization required)
Assurance / mutuelle / mutualité (prior ACPR authorization required)
OPCVM / FCP / FCPR / SCPI (prior AMF authorization required)
Avocat / notaire / huissier / expert-comptable / commissaire aux comptes (reserved regulated professions)
Chambre de commerce / bourse / ordre des avocats (state-protected institutional designations)
République / État / ministère (misleading affiliation with state authority)
Croix-Rouge / ONU / OTAN / UNESCO (internationally protected emblems and names)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory name-reservation register; availability is determined at the moment of filing through the INPI Guichet unique. Upon rejection by the greffe (confusing similarity, prohibited token, or regulatory conflict), the applicant may: (1) amend the draft articles and re-file electronically without prejudice; (2) within 15 days of the refusal, refer the matter to the President of the relevant Tribunal de Commerce by summary application (référé) under Art. R.123-92 of the Code de commerce; (3) contest a trademark-based opposition before the INPI and subsequently before the Paris Court of Appeal. For commodity-brand protection, a pre-filing 'certificat de non-confusion' from an intellectual-property counsel is the recommended administrative practice. The 30-day figure above represents the standard validity period of the pre-filing availability opinion used by counsel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. Under Law No. 94-126 of 11 February 1994 (as amended) and Decree No. 2012-1140, an SAS may domicile its registered office with an authorized commercial domiciliation provider (or business incubator) for a maximum of five years, renewable. A physical reception facility and the domiciliation contract must be disclosed to the RCS. ISIC 4631 commodity brokerage is not a regulated activity and therefore qualifies for domiciliation; however, financing banks for grain letters of credit commonly require demonstrated management substance (lease agreement, local managing director, and projected accounts) before opening USD/EUR LC facilities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Approximately 10% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first three years; no sectoral regulator applies because no statutory license is required. Occasional unannounced visits may occur during a corporate tax audit under Art. L.16 B of the Livre des procédures fiscales if VAT credit anomalies arise; the domiciliation provider performs one scheduled annual compliance visit (scheduled, not unannounced).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (Décret n° 2016-230, Annexe; fixed droit de greffe approx. €54.44 plus platform fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of incorporation notice in a journal d'annonces légales (HAB) in the department of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory capped rate per insertion line (approx. €4–€6 per line, departmental tariff)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation agreement with an authorized domiciliation provider (12-month term)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark annual subscription; €25–€70 per month depending on package and location

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register declaration, AML/CFT internal KYC package, and PEP/sanctions screening of all UBOs and managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat compliance fee within the retainer; obligations under CMF Art. L.561-5

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Full KYC extraction and UBO piercing of the corporate shareholder chain (records from French, Chinese, and/or U.S. registries)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate registries and corporate services provider (INPI, HKCR, EDGAR/state filings)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official extract fees at published registry tariffs plus fixed professional research fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of five UBO and corporate documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-document tariff (approx. €15–€40 per apostille; consular fees approx. €60–€150 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat professional fee; official INPI database search free of charge

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-32 on Société par Actions Simplifiée
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de création de la société
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required for SAS; capital is freely set by shareholders and must be fully subscribed and paid up (Article L. 227-1 Code de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The initial Board of Directors of GrainTrade SAS, a French Société par Actions Simplifiée, resolves unanimously as follows: (1) To subscribe to the initial share capital of EUR 1,000, fully paid-up in cash, represented by 1,000 shares of EUR 1 par value each. (2) To adopt the registered office at 123 Rue de la Paix, 75001 Paris, France, for bulk grain brokerage of soybeans and corn. (3) To appoint Mr. Jean Dupont as President, Ms. Marie Curie as Director, and Mr. Pierre Martin as Secretary. (4) To delegate to the President all powers necessary to formalize the incorporation, file with the commercial registry, and conduct business operations. This resolution is adopted on [Date] and shall be filed with the Greffe.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and signing of corporate statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statutes in French detailing share capital, object, registered office, and officers. Have all shareholders sign the acte de souscription and statuts. Submit electronically with scanned documents.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, provide missing documents or request a hearing with the greffe within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of registration, execute the share subscription by transferring funds to the company account. Appoint and accept roles of directors and secretary. Prepare the procès-verbal of board meeting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit additional clarifications or amend if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission and registration at the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed incorporation file including statuts, board resolution, and payment if applicable. Receive the SIREN number and registration certificate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, appeal to the commercial court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale de la Concurrence, de la Consommation et de la Répression des Fraudes (DGCCRF)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Grains are non-hazardous; compliance with general transport and storage environmental standards with no specific wastewater or VOC thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural inspections for any storage facilities; workplace safety clearances per French Labor Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie et des Finances; taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; central business-formalities platform: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Le Guichet Unique).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned French SAS, the statutory representative files the company-creation application through the Guichet Unique, annexing the SAS articles of association, directors' ID/passport evidence, and the non-resident shareholder's corporate documents. The system registers the SAS with INSEE for SIREN/SIRET identification, with DGFiP for corporate income tax, and with the trade register; DGFiP thereafter issues the intra-Community VAT number. The SAS must also obtain a French EORI number from the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) to file customs export declarations before engaging in bulk agricultural commodity trade.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: There is no check-the-box or pass-through election for an SAS under French law. The principal statutory election is the French tax-consolidation regime (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI, available to an SAS parent holding at least 95% of French subsidiaries. A VAT group election (option de groupe TVA) is also available on an EU-harmonized basis. Hybrid mismatch rules under Articles 212 bis A-H CGI are non-elective and mandatory for French taxpayers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France applies no general VAT registration threshold to French-established or non-established taxable persons: registration is mandatory upon the first taxable transaction. The small-business franchise exemption (franchise en base de TVA) is restricted to French-established micro-enterprises with annual turnover below EUR 85,000 for goods and EUR 37,500 for services; it cannot be relied upon for imports, intra-EU acquisitions, or export zero-rated operations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory structured e-invoicing for domestic B2B transactions with phased entry from 1 September 2026, when all taxpayers must be able to receive e-invoices and large/mid-size issuers must transmit through approved dematerialization platforms (PDP) or Chorus Pro. Smaller issuers follow from 1 September 2027. The mandated formats are Factur-X and EDI; B2C transactions require fiscal-data certification (NF 525/NFi 527) for cash registers and sales-management software.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of bulk agricultural goods to a destination outside the EU is eligible for 0% VAT under Article 262-I-1° CGI when the French SAS proves that the goods physically left EU territory within the relevant statutory timeframe and that the right of disposal was transferred to a non-EU buyer. Directly connected services such as handling, cargo loading, and ocean freight supplied to non-EU customers may also be zero-rated under the same proof-of-export rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU) cleared by DGDDI in the EU Export system
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill issued in the exporter's name or irrevocably endorsed to the exporter
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT payment records evidencing settlement of the export sale
Commercial invoice, packing list, and weighing certificate for the bulk grain cargo
Vessel manifest or port-loading certificate corroborating physical exit from EU territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating claims expose the SAS to immediate VAT reassessment, a 40% bad-faith penalty under Article 1729 CGI or 80% for organized fraud under Article 1729-0 bis CGI, monthly late-payment interest of 0.20%, and an extended six-year audit limitation for hidden declarations. DGFiP cross-checks customs exit records, vessel manifests, and inward FX evidence; failure to evidence payment within the 180-day repatriation benchmark or physical exit within the statutory deadline can trigger retrospective clawback and joint liability of the SAS's legal representatives.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains a fully convertible currency regime under EU law and the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. Both current account transactions (including commodity trade settlements) and capital account movements (equity injections, profit remittances) are unrestricted. No prior approval or surrender obligations apply to resident SAS entities. Profit repatriation to foreign shareholders is permitted without quantitative limits, subject only to standard AML/KYC verification and beneficial ownership disclosure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: As an EU member state, France imposes no mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Soybean and yellow corn receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts or converted at market rates. No statutory timeline or conversion ratio applies; voluntary surrender to authorized banks is available but not required. All transactions must comply with anti-money laundering regulations and purpose-of-payment attestation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) authorized under PSD2 by the ACPR are feasible for limited cross-border payment services but unsuitable for core corporate treasury functions. Legal constraints include strict capital requirements, restrictions on holding client funds, and prohibitions on certain payment services for non-EU entities. Large-scale liquidity management and FX hedging require traditional banking rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Initial corporate onboarding for a new SAS account requires physical presence of at least one authorized signatory for KYC interviews, document verification, and signature attestation. Remote account opening is permitted only for subsequent transactions or after initial setup; full remote onboarding is not authorized for primary corporate accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership or control structure inconsistencies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), beneficial ownership declaration form, source-of-wealth documentation, and independent verification of ownership chain
Proof of clean beneficial ownership, transaction purpose attestation, and legal opinion confirming no adverse media or sanctions exposure
Detailed trade contract, commercial invoice, and irrevocable LC documentation demonstrating legitimate bulk grain trading activity

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections use SWIFT MT103 wires addressed to the SAS IBAN with purpose code 'CAPITAL' or 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION'. Verification requires KYC/AML screening, beneficial ownership confirmation, and supporting documentation (share subscription agreement, board resolution). Domestic EUR wires via SEPA are preferred for speed and zero FX conversion; international wires must include full remittance information and purpose attestation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers and irrevocable transferable Letters of Credit (LCs) under UCP 600. Platforms such as TradeIX or direct bank portals facilitate LC issuance. Settlements may be in EUR or USD; all disbursements require matching commercial invoices, packing lists, and phytosanitary certificates for soybeans and yellow corn. Purpose codes must reflect 'GOODS PURCHASE' or 'TRADE SETTLEMENT'.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts (Bilan and Compte de Résultat)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Authorities (Impôts Gouv.fr) and Commercial Registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €1,500; potential company strike-off for non-compliance
Penalties of 0.5% per month of tax due, capped at 5% of tax liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual deadline; update upon material changes in ownership or UBO
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative sanctions and potential fines for AML non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Annual turnover exceeding €800,000 or total assets exceeding €400,000

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain register of beneficial owners; update and file declaration with tax authorities upon shareholding transfers or UBO changes; no fixed annual filing deadline

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 (if below audit thresholds) to 4,000-6,000 USD (if mandatory audit required)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Qualifying small and medium-sized companies may apply 15% to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to applicable capital ownership, fully paid-up capital, and turnover conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 15% reduced rate may apply to qualifying SMEs; no general tax holiday applies to a French SAS engaged in bulk grain trading. Research, innovation, and other incentive credits or regimes require separate eligibility analysis. A qualifying SME may also be liable for the 3.3% social contribution on IS, subject to the statutory allowance and exemptions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward period; annual use is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally available for one year, subject to a EUR 1 million limit and statutory conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (corporate income tax return), with applicable schedules 2050-SD through 2059-SD under the normal regime; filed electronically through EDI-TDFC or the French tax authority's professional online services. A SAS generally files under the normal real-profit regime unless eligible for and validly using another regime.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; four corporate income tax instalments are generally payable during the fiscal year, with an annual balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the filing deadline is generally the second working day after 1 May, subject to the tax authority's published annual calendar and any electronic filing tolerance. The final IS balance is generally payable by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end; for a calendar year, generally 15 May. Instalments are ordinarily due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December for a calendar-year taxpayer, subject to statutory exceptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN, registered office, activity, tax office, fiscal year dates, and tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS's registered particulars and French SIREN. Identify the SAS as the French taxable entity; disclose foreign parent or shareholder information where requested.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the tax-adjusted accounting result and taxable income or tax loss, with adjustments and schedules supporting the computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include the SAS's French taxable results, including appropriately attributable French operations. Apply French tax adjustments and document any cross-border allocation or permanent-establishment position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Normal-regime balance sheet, income statement, fixed assets, provisions, receivables, liabilities, and reconciliation of accounting and taxable results.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the SAS's French books and transactions. Reconcile related-party balances and transactions to supporting records; do not substitute a foreign parent's consolidated figures for the SAS's accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate IS, report applicable reduced-rate treatment, tax credits, instalments, and remaining balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim a reduced rate or credit only where the SAS independently satisfies the relevant French statutory conditions and retains supporting evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report distributions and other information requested by the return, with applicable distribution schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report distributions by the French SAS and separately assess French withholding, treaty eligibility, beneficial ownership, and required declarations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit the return and required schedules electronically through the applicable professional filing channel.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder does not replace the SAS's filing obligation. Maintain a French-compliant mandate, access, and records for the filing representative where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% where a formal notice is not complied with within the applicable period and potentially 80% in cases such as concealed activity. Late payment generally attracts a 5% surcharge. Statutory late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to applicable rules. Inaccurate or incomplete declarations can trigger additional penalties and tax reassessments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Dividends paid by a French company to a nonresident legal entity are generally subject to 25% French withholding tax, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. Dividends paid to nonresident individuals are generally subject to 12.8%, subject to applicable treaty relief and rules. The EU Parent-Subsidiary regime may exempt qualifying distributions to an eligible EU parent, subject to ownership, holding-period, beneficial-owner, anti-abuse, and filing conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, establish the recipient's treaty residence, beneficial ownership, eligibility, and entitlement under the relevant France tax treaty. Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the competent foreign tax authority and complete the applicable French treaty-relief forms, commonly Form 5000 and the relevant income-specific Form 5001 series for dividends, interest, or royalties. Submit documents to the French payer or tax authority as required. Relief may be applied at source when procedural conditions are met; otherwise, withholding is generally made at the domestic rate and a refund claim may be filed within the applicable limitation period. Treaty benefits are fact- and treaty-specific and subject to principal-purpose, anti-abuse, and beneficial-ownership rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound royalties to nonresidents are generally subject to French withholding at the applicable domestic rate, generally 25%, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and EU law where applicable. Interest paid to nonresidents is generally not subject to French withholding, subject to exceptions, including payments to recipients in non-cooperative states and applicable anti-abuse rules; payments to a non-cooperative state may attract a 75% rate. Treaty rates and exemptions depend on the recipient, instrument, beneficial ownership, and applicable treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Comprehensive transfer-pricing documentation under French Tax Code Article L.13 AA is generally required where the French entity or qualifying group meets the EUR 400 million threshold for annual turnover or gross assets, or falls within specified ownership or control relationships with an entity meeting that threshold. A separate simplified annual transfer-pricing declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies where the French entity or qualifying group meets the EUR 50 million threshold for annual turnover or gross assets, subject to statutory scope and exceptions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not impose a general standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. French anti-abuse, transfer-pricing, permanent-establishment, beneficial-ownership, controlled-foreign-company, and management-and-control rules can nevertheless challenge structures lacking genuine commercial purpose, adequate functions, assets, personnel, or decision-making. Maintain contemporaneous evidence of the SAS's actual trading functions, contracting, pricing, inventory and logistics risks, financing, and decision-making.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional omission of taxable income, fabricated invoices, false accounting, concealed transactions, or deliberate failure to file or pay French tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, interest, and surcharges may apply. Individual tax fraud can be punishable by up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, with higher penalties for aggravated conduct; criminal fines may be increased by reference to proceeds under applicable law. Corporate criminal penalties may apply where statutory attribution requirements are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face personal criminal prosecution and fines where they knowingly participate. A court may impose asset-related or professional sanctions where authorized. Civil tax liability may be imposed on a director in cases of fraud or serious and repeated non-compliance under applicable law; imprisonment or travel restrictions are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing misstatement and undocumented related-party dealings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length pricing, unsupported management or financing charges, profit shifting, failure to provide required documentation, or inaccurate Form 2257-SD or related disclosures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable profits may be adjusted, with interest and applicable penalties. Failure to provide required documentation may trigger a penalty generally subject to a minimum of EUR 10,000 per audited fiscal year and statutory percentage-based limits linked to reassessed amounts or transactions, depending on the violation and applicable provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil or criminal exposure if they knowingly authorize fraudulent arrangements or false filings. Ordinary transfer-pricing adjustments do not automatically create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payment or crediting of dividends, interest, or royalties without applying, reporting, or remitting required French withholding tax, or claiming treaty relief without adequate entitlement evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for unpaid withholding tax, late-payment interest, and applicable surcharges or penalties. Treaty relief may be denied and withholding recovered where residence, beneficial ownership, or anti-abuse conditions are not established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers may face personal exposure for intentional evasion or other qualifying misconduct. The SAS remains primarily responsible as withholding agent, subject to statutory recourse and director-liability rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell arrangements, sham transactions, or abuse of law
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or using entities, contracts, invoices, or ownership arrangements without genuine substance or primarily to obtain an improper tax advantage, including artificial allocation of grain-trading profits or risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may disregard or recharacterize arrangements under applicable French abuse-of-law and anti-abuse provisions, reassess tax, and apply interest and enhanced penalties where statutory conditions are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable where they knowingly implement fraudulent conduct or satisfy statutory civil-liability standards. No general automatic piercing of the corporate veil or automatic travel ban applies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to keep reliable French accounting records, issue compliant invoices, retain supporting documents, or substantiate commodity purchases, sales, freight, insurance, and financing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable income may be assessed by estimation or rejected deductions, with tax, interest, and applicable penalties. Separate accounting, VAT, and commercial-law sanctions may apply depending on the breach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil or criminal consequences for deliberate falsification, destruction of records, or knowingly approved false accounts. Routine record deficiencies do not automatically create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly concealing criminal proceeds, using false trade documentation, disguising counterparties or beneficial owners, or processing prohibited transactions through letters of credit or wire transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering may attract substantial criminal fines and imprisonment under French law; applicable financial sanctions may also prohibit or freeze transactions and assets. Consequences depend on the offence, intent, proceeds, and relevant sanctions regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who knowingly participate may face personal criminal prosecution, fines, imprisonment, and confiscation. Director status alone does not establish liability; travel restrictions require a specific legal basis or court measure.
